summary: Defines the ChaCha20 stream cipher and the Poly1305 authenticator, both on their own and combined as an authenticated encryption (AEAD) algorithm. It replaces RFC 7539, which was a stable reference and implementation guide from the Crypto Forum Research Group.

plainLanguage.summary: ChaCha20 hides message contents, while Poly1305 creates a tag that helps detect changes. RFC 8439 specifies both algorithms and a combined method that encrypts data and checks its integrity.

questions: why use chacha20 instead of aes
subtitle: A stream cipher and message authenticator combined for authenticated encryption.

tldr.problem: Protocols need a clear specification for encryption and message authentication, including a choice beyond AES for platforms without dedicated AES hardware.
tldr.mechanism: ChaCha20 produces a keystream for encryption. Poly1305 creates an authentication tag, and the AEAD construction combines them to protect ciphertext and associated data.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8439 is an Informational reference that replaces RFC 7539 and incorporates its filed errata. It includes test vectors and implementation guidance.

today: RFC 8439 is an Informational RFC that obsoletes RFC 7539. It merges the errata filed against that document and adds text to its Security Considerations.

sections.title: Three Related Algorithms
sections.content:
RFC 8439 defines ChaCha20, Poly1305, and their combination, AEAD_CHACHA20_POLY1305. The RFC presents these algorithms as a stable reference and implementation guide for IETF documents, not as newly invented algorithms.

The introduction says ChaCha20 can be faster than the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) in software-only implementations and describes AES cache-collision timing attacks as a concern for some implementations. The document replaces RFC 7539, merges its filed errata, and adds text to the Security Considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC specifies one method for hiding data and another for checking it. It also explains how to combine them and gives test examples for implementers.

sections.title: ChaCha20 and Poly1305
sections.content:
ChaCha20 uses a 256-bit key, a 96-bit nonce, and a block counter to produce 64-byte blocks of keystream. It combines that stream with plaintext using XOR; applying the same operation to ciphertext recovers the plaintext. The counter advances for each block.

Poly1305 takes a 32-byte one-time key and a message, then produces a 16-byte tag. The key must be unique and unpredictable for each use. The RFC also defines how ChaCha20 can generate the one-time Poly1305 key.
sections.plainLanguage: ChaCha20 makes a stream of bytes that can hide a message when combined with it. Poly1305 makes a short tag from a message so a receiver can check whether it changed.

sections.title: Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data
sections.content:
AEAD_CHACHA20_POLY1305 takes a 256-bit key, a 96-bit nonce, plaintext, and optional additional authenticated data (AAD). It derives a one-time Poly1305 key, encrypts the plaintext with ChaCha20, then authenticates the AAD and ciphertext with Poly1305.

The result is ciphertext followed by a 128-bit tag. During decryption, the receiver checks the tag against the AAD and ciphertext; the plaintext is accepted only when the tags match. A nonce must differ for each invocation that uses the same key.
sections.plainLanguage: The combined method encrypts the message and makes a tag for both the encrypted data and optional associated data. The receiver checks the tag before accepting the message.

sections.title: Implementation and Security Rules
sections.content:
Reusing a nonce with the same key repeats both the keystream and the Poly1305 key, which can reveal the XOR of the plaintexts. Implementations need unique nonces and an unpredictable one-time Poly1305 key.

The RFC says implementations should use constant-time operations to reduce timing leaks. Online protocols must compare tags in constant time and must include the complete tag; tag truncation is not allowed. Generic big-number libraries may not provide constant-time Poly1305 operations.
sections.plainLanguage: Never repeat a nonce with the same key. Check the complete tag in constant time so timing differences do not reveal information.
